mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Hirschsprung disease is congenital aganglionosis of the distal rectum/colon causing functional intestinal obstruction, failure to pass meconium in first 48 hrs, and abdominal distension.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the hallmark clinical presentation of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in a 4-week-old male infant?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the hallmark clinical presentation of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in a 4-week-old male infant?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.optionA: Bile-stained green vomiting and currant jelly stools

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Pyloric stenosis presents at 3–6 weeks with non-bilious projectile vomiting, visible gastric peristaltic waves, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, and a palpable epigastric olive mass.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: IMNCI fast breathing thresholds: < 2 months = ≥ 60 breaths/min; 2 to 11 months = ≥ 50 breaths/min; 12 months to 5 years = ≥ 40 breaths/min.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Viral croup (parainfluenza) causes subglottic tracheal narrowing producing the characteristic "Steeple sign" on frontal neck radiograph, barking cough, and nocturnal stridor.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: The classic "3 Cs" of TEF are Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis during feedings, accompanied by excessive frothy salivation and drooling from the mouth.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under BMW rules, contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as used IV tubing, Foley catheters, urine bags, and disposable syringes (without needles) must be disposed of in which color bin?

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.optionB: Meticulous hand hygiene (5 moments of hand hygiene)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.optionD: Wearing double gloves for all procedures
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: WHO and CDC establish that proper hand hygiene (alcohol rub for 20–30s or soap & water for 40–60s) is the primary, most cost-effective measure to eliminate pathogen cross-transmission.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the gold standard method to definitively confirm correct placement of a newly inserted nasogastric (NG) tube before initiating enteral feeds or medications?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the gold standard method to definitively confirm correct placement of a newly inserted nasogastric (NG) tube before initiating enteral feeds or medications?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.optionA: Auscultating air insufflation over the epigastrium with a stethoscope
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.optionD: Immersing the tube tip in water to watch for bubbles
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: An abdominal/chest X-ray visualizing the tube tip in the stomach below the diaphragm is the absolute gold standard before any feed. Auscultation is unreliable and unsafe.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Left lateral Sims’ position (lying on left side with right knee flexed) aligns with anatomical curvature of sigmoid colon and descending colon, facilitating fluid entry.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.optionD: No impact on BP reading accuracy

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: A cuff bladder that is too narrow or wrapped too loosely requires excessive cuff inflation pressure to compress the brachial artery, yielding falsely elevated BP readings.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: The Z-track technique displaces skin and subcutaneous tissue laterally before injection, sealing the medication track in the muscle layer upon needle withdrawal and preventing leakage/skin staining.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Beneficence is the ethical duty to do good and promote patient well-being. Non-maleficence is the duty to do no harm; Autonomy is respecting patient decision-making rights.

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: CRPF Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Central Reserve Police Force Official Syllabus Model Paper)

mock-crpf-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In a Mass Casualty Incident (START Triage system), a victim who is non-ambulatory, has respiratory rate of 24/min, radial pulse present, and obeys commands should be assigned which triage tag color?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: In a Mass Casualty Incident (START Triage system), a victim who is non-ambulatory, has respiratory rate of 24/min, radial pulse present, and obeys commands should be assigned which triage tag color?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the characteristic ECG appearance of complete third-degree Atrioventricular (AV) heart block?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.optionC: Fixed prolonged PR interval > 0.20 seconds with 1:1 conduction

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: According to Naegele’s rule, what is the expected date of delivery (EDD) for a pregnant woman whose Last Menstrual Period (LMP) was 10 October 2025?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: According to Naegele’s rule, what is the expected date of delivery (EDD) for a pregnant woman whose Last Menstrual Period (LMP) was 10 October 2025?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Naegele’s Rule = LMP + 7 days - 3 months + 1 year. 10 October + 7 days = 17 October; minus 3 months = 17 July 2026.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.optionA: Absence of deep tendon reflexes (Patellar reflex)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Loss of deep tendon reflexes (patellar reflex) is the earliest clinical sign of hypermagnesemia (serum Mg 8–10 mEq/L), preceding respiratory depression (<12/min) and cardiac arrest (>15 mEq/L).

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific, life-saving antidote administered for acute Magnesium Sulfate toxicity in an obstetric patient?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: 10% Calcium Gluconate (1 g in 10 mL IV push over 3–5 minutes) acts as a direct physiologic antagonist to magnesium at the neuromuscular junction.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the primary frontline drug of choice recommended by WHO guidelines for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) to prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the primary frontline drug of choice recommended by WHO guidelines for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) to prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Oxytocin 10 IU IM (or slow IV) immediately after delivery of the baby is the global gold standard uterotonic for AMTSL due to its rapid onset and absence of hypertensive side effects.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A postpartum mother on day 3 post-delivery exhibits normal vaginal discharge that is pinkish-brown in color composed of serous exudate, erythrocytes, and leukocytes. What is this lochia called?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: During fetal heart rate monitoring, late decelerations are observed following uterine contractions. What is the underlying pathophysiological cause?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At which gestational age does the uterine fundus normally reach the level of the maternal umbilicus in a singleton pregnancy?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Chadwick’s sign is bluish/violet discoloration of vulva/vagina/cervix at ~6–8 weeks. Goodell’s sign is cervical softening; Hegar’s sign is softening of the lower uterine isthmus.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: The anterior diamond-shaped fontanelle closes between 12 and 18 months of age. The posterior triangular fontanelle (Lambda) closes much earlier, between 6 and 8 weeks (2 months).

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.optionD: Wearing double gloves for all procedures

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Left lateral Sims’ position (lying on left side with right knee flexed) aligns with anatomical curvature of sigmoid colon and descending colon, facilitating fluid entry.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: A cuff bladder that is too narrow or wrapped too loosely requires excessive cuff inflation pressure to compress the brachial artery, yielding falsely elevated BP readings.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: The Z-track technique displaces skin and subcutaneous tissue laterally before injection, sealing the medication track in the muscle layer upon needle withdrawal and preventing leakage/skin staining.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Beneficence is the ethical duty to do good and promote patient well-being. Non-maleficence is the duty to do no harm; Autonomy is respecting patient decision-making rights.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: If a nurse makes an erroneous entry in a manual hospital medical chart, what is the legally correct documentation procedure to rectify the mistake?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Ringer Lactate has an electrolyte composition closest to human plasma (Na 130, K 4, Ca 2.7, Cl 109, Lactate 28 mEq/L) and is the frontline crystalloid for shock resuscitation.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Dose = 5 × 70 = 350 mcg/min = 21,000 mcg/hr = 21 mg/hr. Concentration = 400 mg / 250 mL = 1.6 mg/mL. Rate = 21 / 1.6 = 13.125 ≈ 13.1 mL/hr.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Drip rate = (Total Volume in mL × Drop Factor) / Time in Minutes = (1000 × 15) / (8 × 60) = 15,000 / 480 = 31.25 ≈ 31 drops/min.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Protamine sulfate is a strongly basic polycationic peptide that binds ionically to acidic Heparin to form an inactive stable salt complex.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Naloxone is a pure mu-opioid receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression, sedation, and coma.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: N-Acetylcysteine replenishes hepatic glutathione stores, neutralizing the toxic paracetamol metabolite NAPQI (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine).

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Atropine competitively blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors to reverse bronchial secretions and bradycardia, while Pralidoxime reactivates inhibited acetylcholinesterase enzyme.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with Bipolar Disorder is prescribed Lithium Carbonate. What is the narrow therapeutic serum range for maintenance lithium therapy?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with Bipolar Disorder is prescribed Lithium Carbonate. What is the narrow therapeutic serum range for maintenance lithium therapy?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Therapeutic lithium range is 0.6–1.2 mEq/L. Levels > 1.5 mEq/L produce early toxicity (vomiting, coarse tremors, ataxia), and > 2.0 mEq/L can cause seizures, coma, and death.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs is most notorious for causing peripheral neuropathy, which can be prevented by co-prescribing Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs is most notorious for causing peripheral neuropathy, which can be prevented by co-prescribing Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Isoniazid (INH) interferes with vitamin B6 metabolism, leading to dose-dependent peripheral neuropathy. Co-administration of 10–25 mg/day Pyridoxine prevents this adverse effect.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which anti-tubercular medication causes retrobulbar optic neuritis leading to decreased visual acuity and loss of green-red color discrimination?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which anti-tubercular medication causes retrobulbar optic neuritis leading to decreased visual acuity and loss of green-red color discrimination?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Ethambutol (mnemonic: "E" for Eye) is known for ocular toxicity (optic neuritis). Monthly visual acuity and Ishihara color discrimination testing is mandatory.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the primary mechanism of action of Heparin in preventing thrombus formation?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the primary mechanism of action of Heparin in preventing thrombus formation?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.optionA: Accelerating the inhibitory action of Antithrombin III against Thrombin and Factor Xa
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.optionB: Direct inhibition of Vitamin K epoxide reductase
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Recruitment Wing Official Key)
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Heparin binds to antithrombin III, inducing a conformational change that accelerates its inhibition of activated thrombin (Factor IIa) and Factor Xa by over 1000-fold.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the National Immunization Schedule (NIS) of India, what is the exact dose and route for administering BCG vaccine to a neonate at birth?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At which temperature range must the vaccine cold chain be strictly maintained inside Ice-Lined Refrigerators (ILR) for sensitive vaccines like OPV, Measles, and Pentavalent?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is epidemiologically expressed as the number of maternal deaths per how many live births in a given year?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Indian public health norms: Sub-centre = 5,000 (Plain) / 3,000 (Hilly); PHC = 30,000 (Plain) / 20,000 (Hilly); CHC = 120,000 (Plain) / 80,000 (Hilly).

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following defense mechanisms involves redirecting unacceptable impulses, anger, or aggressive feelings toward a less threatening, safer substitute target?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the frontline pharmacological agent prescribed for acute alcohol withdrawal to prevent delirium tremens and withdrawal seizures?
pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the frontline pharmacological agent prescribed for acute alcohol withdrawal to prevent delirium tremens and withdrawal seizures?

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.explanation: Long-acting benzodiazepines provide cross-tolerance to alcohol at GABA-A receptors, stabilizing autonomic hyperactivity and preventing withdrawal seizures and delirium tremens.

pyq-sctimst-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Wernicke-Korsakoff encephalopathy in chronic alcoholism is caused by a severe dietary deficiency of which essential vitamin?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Within 10 minutes of starting a Packed Red Blood Cell (PRBC) transfusion, the patient develops chills, fever, lower back pain, and dark burgundy urine. What is the nurse’s immediate first action?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: A young adult with a long bone femur fracture suddenly develops dyspnea, confusion, tachypnea, and petechial rash over the chest and conjunctiva 24 hours post-trauma. What syndrome should the nurse suspect?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: In a Mass Casualty Incident (START Triage system), a victim who is non-ambulatory, has respiratory rate of 24/min, radial pulse present, and obeys commands should be assigned which triage tag color?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: According to Naegele’s rule, what is the expected date of delivery (EDD) for a pregnant woman whose Last Menstrual Period (LMP) was 10 October 2025?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: SCTIMST Thiruvananthapuram Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (SCTIMST Kerala Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Naegele’s Rule = LMP + 7 days - 3 months + 1 year. 10 October + 7 days = 17 October; minus 3 months = 17 July 2026.

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?
mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Loss of deep tendon reflexes (patellar reflex) is the earliest clinical sign of hypermagnesemia (serum Mg 8–10 mEq/L), preceding respiratory depression (<12/min) and cardiac arrest (>15 mEq/L).

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific, life-saving antidote administered for acute Magnesium Sulfate toxicity in an obstetric patient?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: 10% Calcium Gluconate (1 g in 10 mL IV push over 3–5 minutes) acts as a direct physiologic antagonist to magnesium at the neuromuscular junction.

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the primary frontline drug of choice recommended by WHO guidelines for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) to prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Oxytocin 10 IU IM (or slow IV) immediately after delivery of the baby is the global gold standard uterotonic for AMTSL due to its rapid onset and absence of hypertensive side effects.

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: The anterior diamond-shaped fontanelle closes between 12 and 18 months of age. The posterior triangular fontanelle (Lambda) closes much earlier, between 6 and 8 weeks (2 months).

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextDisplay: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?

mock-sctimst-nurse-2026-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At which gestational age does the uterine fundus normally reach the level of the maternal umbilicus in a singleton pregnancy?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.answerSource: NEIGRIHMS Shillong Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (NEIGRIHMS Examination Cell Master Key)

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: The anterior diamond-shaped fontanelle closes between 12 and 18 months of age. The posterior triangular fontanelle (Lambda) closes much earlier, between 6 and 8 weeks (2 months).

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: Hirschsprung disease is congenital aganglionosis of the distal rectum/colon causing functional intestinal obstruction, failure to pass meconium in first 48 hrs, and abdominal distension.

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the hallmark clinical presentation of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in a 4-week-old male infant?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.optionA: Bile-stained green vomiting and currant jelly stools

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: IMNCI fast breathing thresholds: < 2 months = ≥ 60 breaths/min; 2 to 11 months = ≥ 50 breaths/min; 12 months to 5 years = ≥ 40 breaths/min.

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: Viral croup (parainfluenza) causes subglottic tracheal narrowing producing the characteristic "Steeple sign" on frontal neck radiograph, barking cough, and nocturnal stridor.

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: Dose = 5 × 70 = 350 mcg/min = 21,000 mcg/hr = 21 mg/hr. Concentration = 400 mg / 250 mL = 1.6 mg/mL. Rate = 21 / 1.6 = 13.125 ≈ 13.1 mL/hr.

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: Drip rate = (Total Volume in mL × Drop Factor) / Time in Minutes = (1000 × 15) / (8 × 60) = 15,000 / 480 = 31.25 ≈ 31 drops/min.

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: Naloxone is a pure mu-opioid receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression, sedation, and coma.

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.answerSource: NEIGRIHMS Shillong Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (NEIGRIHMS Examination Cell Master Key)
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: N-Acetylcysteine replenishes hepatic glutathione stores, neutralizing the toxic paracetamol metabolite NAPQI (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine).

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: Atropine competitively blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors to reverse bronchial secretions and bradycardia, while Pralidoxime reactivates inhibited acetylcholinesterase enzyme.

pyq-neigrihms-nurse-2026.explanation: Therapeutic lithium range is 0.6–1.2 mEq/L. Levels > 1.5 mEq/L produce early toxicity (vomiting, coarse tremors, ataxia), and > 2.0 mEq/L can cause seizures, coma, and death.

mock-neigrihms-nurse-2026-2026.answerSource: NEIGRIHMS Shillong Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (NEIGRIHMS Shillong Official Syllabus Model Paper)
mock-neigrihms-nurse-2026-2026.explanation: Naegele’s Rule = LMP + 7 days - 3 months + 1 year. 10 October + 7 days = 17 October; minus 3 months = 17 July 2026.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Acute allograft rejection manifests as oliguria, progressive rise in serum creatinine/BUN, graft site tenderness/swelling, fever, and fluid retention.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient on mechanical ventilation suddenly develops High Peak Pressure alarms, absent breath sounds on the left, contralateral tracheal deviation to the right, and blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg. What is the immediate priority action?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient on mechanical ventilation suddenly develops High Peak Pressure alarms, absent breath sounds on the left, contralateral tracheal deviation to the right, and blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg. What is the immediate priority action?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Perform immediate needle thoracostomy decompression at the 2nd intercostal space
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionC: Obtain an urgent portable chest X-ray
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Tension pneumothorax is an immediate clinical emergency. Decompression with a 14G/16G needle at 2nd intercostal space midclavicular line (or 4th/5th ICS anterior axillary line) must not await X-ray confirmation.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Within 10 minutes of starting a Packed Red Blood Cell (PRBC) transfusion, the patient develops chills, fever, lower back pain, and dark burgundy urine. What is the nurse’s immediate first action?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Within 10 minutes of starting a Packed Red Blood Cell (PRBC) transfusion, the patient develops chills, fever, lower back pain, and dark burgundy urine. What is the nurse’s immediate first action?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Slow down the infusion rate and administer IV Paracetamol
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionB: Stop the blood transfusion immediately and infuse 0.9% Normal Saline via fresh tubing
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionC: Administer IV Diphenhydramine and monitor for 15 minutes
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionD: Elevate the patient’s legs and record vital signs
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: These symptoms indicate an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (ABO incompatibility). The transfusion must be stopped immediately to halt antigen load, maintaining IV access with fresh NS tubing.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the maximum approved therapeutic window for administering intravenous recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (IV rt-PA / Alteplase) from symptom onset in acute ischemic stroke?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the maximum approved therapeutic window for administering intravenous recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (IV rt-PA / Alteplase) from symptom onset in acute ischemic stroke?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Standard clinical guidelines (AHA/ASA) approve IV thrombolysis with rt-PA within 3 to 4.5 hours of documented ischemic stroke symptom onset in eligible patients without contraindications.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) of an adult in cardiac arrest, what is the correct compression-to-ventilation ratio for a single rescuer without an advanced airway?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) of an adult in cardiac arrest, what is the correct compression-to-ventilation ratio for a single rescuer without an advanced airway?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionD: Continuous compressions with 1 breath every 15 seconds
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: AHA/ERC guidelines mandate a compression-to-ventilation ratio of 30:2 at a depth of 5–6 cm and rate of 100–120 compressions/min for all single-rescuer adult CPR.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with chronic CO2 retention requires supplemental oxygen. Which delivery device and target SpO2 range is most appropriate?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with chronic CO2 retention requires supplemental oxygen. Which delivery device and target SpO2 range is most appropriate?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionB: Venturi mask titrated to maintain SpO2 88%–92%
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Patients with chronic hypercapnia rely on hypoxic drive. Controlled low-flow oxygen via a Venturi mask targeting SpO2 88–92% prevents worsening hypercapnic respiratory failure and CO2 narcosis.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A young adult with a long bone femur fracture suddenly develops dyspnea, confusion, tachypnea, and petechial rash over the chest and conjunctiva 24 hours post-trauma. What syndrome should the nurse suspect?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A young adult with a long bone femur fracture suddenly develops dyspnea, confusion, tachypnea, and petechial rash over the chest and conjunctiva 24 hours post-trauma. What syndrome should the nurse suspect?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: The classic triad of respiratory distress, neurological changes (confusion), and non-palpable petechial rash on anterior thorax/axillae following long bone fracture defines Fat Embolism Syndrome.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following is the definitive diagnostic test for confirming active pulmonary tuberculosis according to WHO / NTEP guidelines?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: GeneXpert/CBNAAT provides rapid, automated molecular detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA and simultaneously tests for Rifampicin resistance within 2 hours.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient receiving IV Doxorubicin (Adriamycin) requires baseline and periodic monitoring of which organ function due to known drug toxicity?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient receiving IV Doxorubicin (Adriamycin) requires baseline and periodic monitoring of which organ function due to known drug toxicity?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Anthracyclines like Doxorubicin cause cumulative dose-dependent cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure, necessitating baseline and serial echocardiogram evaluations.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In a Mass Casualty Incident (START Triage system), a victim who is non-ambulatory, has respiratory rate of 24/min, radial pulse present, and obeys commands should be assigned which triage tag color?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: In a Mass Casualty Incident (START Triage system), a victim who is non-ambulatory, has respiratory rate of 24/min, radial pulse present, and obeys commands should be assigned which triage tag color?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: START Triage: Respiration < 30, Perfusion (radial pulse present / cap refill < 2s), Mental status (obeys commands) = Yellow (Delayed / Urgent but not immediate life threat).

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the characteristic ECG appearance of complete third-degree Atrioventricular (AV) heart block?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the characteristic ECG appearance of complete third-degree Atrioventricular (AV) heart block?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Progressive prolongation of PR interval followed by a dropped QRS complex
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionB: Complete dissociation between regular P waves and regular independent QRS complexes
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionC: Fixed prolonged PR interval > 0.20 seconds with 1:1 conduction
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionD: Sawtooth baseline flutter waves at 300 bpm
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: In third-degree (complete) AV block, no atrial impulses conduct to the ventricles. Atria and ventricles beat completely independently (AV dissociation) with separate regular P-P and R-R intervals.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When assessing a patient with an arteriovenous (AV) fistula in the left forearm for hemodialysis, which finding confirms patency of the vascular access?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When assessing a patient with an arteriovenous (AV) fistula in the left forearm for hemodialysis, which finding confirms patency of the vascular access?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Presence of a palpable thrill and audible bruit over the access site
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionB: Radial pulse deficit on the left arm
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionC: Blood pressure higher in the left arm
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: A palpable vibration (thrill) and a continuous rushing sound on auscultation (bruit) indicate turbulent, high-velocity arterial-venous blood flow confirming fistula patency.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A primigravida at 34 weeks gestation presents with sudden painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. Her vitals are stable and fetal heart rate is 144 bpm. Which nursing action is strictly contraindicated?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A primigravida at 34 weeks gestation presents with sudden painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. Her vitals are stable and fetal heart rate is 144 bpm. Which nursing action is strictly contraindicated?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Continuous external fetal heart rate monitoring
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionB: Establishing wide-bore IV access with Ringer Lactate
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionC: Performing a digital vaginal examination (P/V examination)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionD: Obtaining an urgent obstetric transabdominal ultrasound
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: In suspected placenta previa (painless bright red bleeding in third trimester), digital vaginal examination is strictly contraindicated as finger insertion can disrupt placental attachments and trigger catastrophic hemorrhage.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: According to Naegele’s rule, what is the expected date of delivery (EDD) for a pregnant woman whose Last Menstrual Period (LMP) was 10 October 2025?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: According to Naegele’s rule, what is the expected date of delivery (EDD) for a pregnant woman whose Last Menstrual Period (LMP) was 10 October 2025?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Naegele’s Rule = LMP + 7 days - 3 months + 1 year. 10 October + 7 days = 17 October; minus 3 months = 17 July 2026.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Absence of deep tendon reflexes (Patellar reflex)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Loss of deep tendon reflexes (patellar reflex) is the earliest clinical sign of hypermagnesemia (serum Mg 8–10 mEq/L), preceding respiratory depression (<12/min) and cardiac arrest (>15 mEq/L).

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific, life-saving antidote administered for acute Magnesium Sulfate toxicity in an obstetric patient?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific, life-saving antidote administered for acute Magnesium Sulfate toxicity in an obstetric patient?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Calcium Gluconate 10% IV (10 mL slowly over 5–10 minutes)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: 10% Calcium Gluconate (1 g in 10 mL IV push over 3–5 minutes) acts as a direct physiologic antagonist to magnesium at the neuromuscular junction.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the primary frontline drug of choice recommended by WHO guidelines for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) to prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the primary frontline drug of choice recommended by WHO guidelines for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) to prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Oxytocin 10 IU IM (or slow IV) immediately after delivery of the baby is the global gold standard uterotonic for AMTSL due to its rapid onset and absence of hypertensive side effects.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A postpartum mother on day 3 post-delivery exhibits normal vaginal discharge that is pinkish-brown in color composed of serous exudate, erythrocytes, and leukocytes. What is this lochia called?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A postpartum mother on day 3 post-delivery exhibits normal vaginal discharge that is pinkish-brown in color composed of serous exudate, erythrocytes, and leukocytes. What is this lochia called?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Lochia progression: Lochia Rubra (Days 1–3, red blood); Lochia Serosa (Days 4–10, pink/brownish serous); Lochia Alba (Days 10–21, yellowish-white mucus/leukocytes).

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: During fetal heart rate monitoring, late decelerations are observed following uterine contractions. What is the underlying pathophysiological cause?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: During fetal heart rate monitoring, late decelerations are observed following uterine contractions. What is the underlying pathophysiological cause?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: VEAL CHOP mnemonic: Variable = Cord compression; Early = Head compression; Accelerations = Ok; Late decelerations = Placental insufficiency requiring left lateral positioning, O2, and stopping oxytocin.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A postpartum nurse discovers umbilical cord prolapse protruding through the introitus after membrane rupture. What is the immediate priority nursing action?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A postpartum nurse discovers umbilical cord prolapse protruding through the introitus after membrane rupture. What is the immediate priority nursing action?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Manual upward elevation of the fetal presenting part relieves vascular compression on the prolapsed cord until an emergency cesarean section can be performed.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At which gestational age does the uterine fundus normally reach the level of the maternal umbilicus in a singleton pregnancy?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: At which gestational age does the uterine fundus normally reach the level of the maternal umbilicus in a singleton pregnancy?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Fundal height landmarks: Symphysis pubis = 12 weeks; Midway between pubis & umbilicus = 16 weeks; Umbilicus = 20–22 weeks; Xiphisternum = 36 weeks.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Chadwick’s sign is bluish/violet discoloration of vulva/vagina/cervix at ~6–8 weeks. Goodell’s sign is cervical softening; Hegar’s sign is softening of the lower uterine isthmus.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Heart rate > 100 (2) + Slow irregular resp (1) + Active flexed tone (2) + Vigorous cry (2) + Acrocyanosis (1) = Total APGAR = 8.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: The anterior diamond-shaped fontanelle closes between 12 and 18 months of age. The posterior triangular fontanelle (Lambda) closes much earlier, between 6 and 8 weeks (2 months).

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Gross motor milestones: Holds neck steady = 3 months; Sits with support = 5–6 months; Sits without support = 8 months; Stands with support = 9 months; Walks independently = 12–15 months.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: During phototherapy for neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which two anatomical areas MUST be shielded and protected from light exposure at all times?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: During phototherapy for neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which two anatomical areas MUST be shielded and protected from light exposure at all times?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Hirschsprung disease is congenital aganglionosis of the distal rectum/colon causing functional intestinal obstruction, failure to pass meconium in first 48 hrs, and abdominal distension.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the hallmark clinical presentation of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in a 4-week-old male infant?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the hallmark clinical presentation of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in a 4-week-old male infant?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Pyloric stenosis presents at 3–6 weeks with non-bilious projectile vomiting, visible gastric peristaltic waves, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, and a palpable epigastric olive mass.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: IMNCI fast breathing thresholds: < 2 months = ≥ 60 breaths/min; 2 to 11 months = ≥ 50 breaths/min; 12 months to 5 years = ≥ 40 breaths/min.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Viral croup (parainfluenza) causes subglottic tracheal narrowing producing the characteristic "Steeple sign" on frontal neck radiograph, barking cough, and nocturnal stridor.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: The classic "3 Cs" of TEF are Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis during feedings, accompanied by excessive frothy salivation and drooling from the mouth.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: According to the revised Bio-Medical Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, in which colored container/bag should human anatomical tissue, placenta, and blood-soaked cotton gauze dressings be segregated?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: According to the revised Bio-Medical Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, in which colored container/bag should human anatomical tissue, placenta, and blood-soaked cotton gauze dressings be segregated?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Yellow bags are strictly designated for incinerable organic/pathological wastes: human anatomical tissues, organs, placenta, soiled cotton dressings, and expired cytotoxic drugs.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under BMW rules, contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as used IV tubing, Foley catheters, urine bags, and disposable syringes (without needles) must be disposed of in which color bin?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under BMW rules, contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as used IV tubing, Foley catheters, urine bags, and disposable syringes (without needles) must be disposed of in which color bin?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionB: Meticulous hand hygiene (5 moments of hand hygiene)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionD: Wearing double gloves for all procedures
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: WHO and CDC establish that proper hand hygiene (alcohol rub for 20–30s or soap & water for 40–60s) is the primary, most cost-effective measure to eliminate pathogen cross-transmission.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the gold standard method to definitively confirm correct placement of a newly inserted nasogastric (NG) tube before initiating enteral feeds or medications?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the gold standard method to definitively confirm correct placement of a newly inserted nasogastric (NG) tube before initiating enteral feeds or medications?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionA: Auscultating air insufflation over the epigastrium with a stethoscope
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.optionD: Immersing the tube tip in water to watch for bubbles
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: An abdominal/chest X-ray visualizing the tube tip in the stomach below the diaphragm is the absolute gold standard before any feed. Auscultation is unreliable and unsafe.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Left lateral Sims’ position (lying on left side with right knee flexed) aligns with anatomical curvature of sigmoid colon and descending colon, facilitating fluid entry.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: A cuff bladder that is too narrow or wrapped too loosely requires excessive cuff inflation pressure to compress the brachial artery, yielding falsely elevated BP readings.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: The Z-track technique displaces skin and subcutaneous tissue laterally before injection, sealing the medication track in the muscle layer upon needle withdrawal and preventing leakage/skin staining.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.answerSource: UPPSC Staff Nurse (Male/Female) Master Answer Key (UPPSC Advt A-3/E-1/2023 Final Answer Key)
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.explanation: Beneficence is the ethical duty to do good and promote patient well-being. Non-maleficence is the duty to do no harm; Autonomy is respecting patient decision-making rights.

pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: If a nurse makes an erroneous entry in a manual hospital medical chart, what is the legally correct documentation procedure to rectify the mistake?
pyq-uppsc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: If a nurse makes an erroneous entry in a manual hospital medical chart, what is the legally correct documentation procedure to rectify the mistake?
