pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Fundal height landmarks: Symphysis pubis = 12 weeks; Midway between pubis & umbilicus = 16 weeks; Umbilicus = 20–22 weeks; Xiphisternum = 36 weeks.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Chadwick’s sign is bluish/violet discoloration of vulva/vagina/cervix at ~6–8 weeks. Goodell’s sign is cervical softening; Hegar’s sign is softening of the lower uterine isthmus.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: The anterior diamond-shaped fontanelle closes between 12 and 18 months of age. The posterior triangular fontanelle (Lambda) closes much earlier, between 6 and 8 weeks (2 months).

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Gross motor milestones: Holds neck steady = 3 months; Sits with support = 5–6 months; Sits without support = 8 months; Stands with support = 9 months; Walks independently = 12–15 months.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Hirschsprung disease is congenital aganglionosis of the distal rectum/colon causing functional intestinal obstruction, failure to pass meconium in first 48 hrs, and abdominal distension.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the hallmark clinical presentation of hypertrophic pyloric stenosis in a 4-week-old male infant?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.optionA: Bile-stained green vomiting and currant jelly stools
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.optionB: Non-bilious projectile vomiting immediately after feeds with palpable olive-shaped abdominal mass
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Pyloric stenosis presents at 3–6 weeks with non-bilious projectile vomiting, visible gastric peristaltic waves, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, and a palpable epigastric olive mass.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: IMNCI fast breathing thresholds: < 2 months = ≥ 60 breaths/min; 2 to 11 months = ≥ 50 breaths/min; 12 months to 5 years = ≥ 40 breaths/min.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Viral croup (parainfluenza) causes subglottic tracheal narrowing producing the characteristic "Steeple sign" on frontal neck radiograph, barking cough, and nocturnal stridor.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: The classic "3 Cs" of TEF are Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis during feedings, accompanied by excessive frothy salivation and drooling from the mouth.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.optionB: Meticulous hand hygiene (5 moments of hand hygiene)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.optionD: Wearing double gloves for all procedures
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: WHO and CDC establish that proper hand hygiene (alcohol rub for 20–30s or soap & water for 40–60s) is the primary, most cost-effective measure to eliminate pathogen cross-transmission.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the gold standard method to definitively confirm correct placement of a newly inserted nasogastric (NG) tube before initiating enteral feeds or medications?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the gold standard method to definitively confirm correct placement of a newly inserted nasogastric (NG) tube before initiating enteral feeds or medications?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: An abdominal/chest X-ray visualizing the tube tip in the stomach below the diaphragm is the absolute gold standard before any feed. Auscultation is unreliable and unsafe.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Left lateral Sims’ position (lying on left side with right knee flexed) aligns with anatomical curvature of sigmoid colon and descending colon, facilitating fluid entry.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.optionD: No impact on BP reading accuracy

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: A cuff bladder that is too narrow or wrapped too loosely requires excessive cuff inflation pressure to compress the brachial artery, yielding falsely elevated BP readings.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: The Z-track technique displaces skin and subcutaneous tissue laterally before injection, sealing the medication track in the muscle layer upon needle withdrawal and preventing leakage/skin staining.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Beneficence is the ethical duty to do good and promote patient well-being. Non-maleficence is the duty to do no harm; Autonomy is respecting patient decision-making rights.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: If a nurse makes an erroneous entry in a manual hospital medical chart, what is the legally correct documentation procedure to rectify the mistake?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Ringer Lactate has an electrolyte composition closest to human plasma (Na 130, K 4, Ca 2.7, Cl 109, Lactate 28 mEq/L) and is the frontline crystalloid for shock resuscitation.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Dose = 5 × 70 = 350 mcg/min = 21,000 mcg/hr = 21 mg/hr. Concentration = 400 mg / 250 mL = 1.6 mg/mL. Rate = 21 / 1.6 = 13.125 ≈ 13.1 mL/hr.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Drip rate = (Total Volume in mL × Drop Factor) / Time in Minutes = (1000 × 15) / (8 × 60) = 15,000 / 480 = 31.25 ≈ 31 drops/min.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Protamine sulfate is a strongly basic polycationic peptide that binds ionically to acidic Heparin to form an inactive stable salt complex.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: Naloxone is a pure mu-opioid receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression, sedation, and coma.

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.answerSource: Goa Medical College Staff Nurse Master Answer Key (Goa GMC Staff Nurse Recruitment Key)
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.explanation: N-Acetylcysteine replenishes hepatic glutathione stores, neutralizing the toxic paracetamol metabolite NAPQI (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine).

pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-goa-gmc-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Naegele’s Rule = LMP + 7 days - 3 months + 1 year. 10 October + 7 days = 17 October; minus 3 months = 17 July 2026.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: The classic "3 Cs" of TEF are Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis during feedings, accompanied by excessive frothy salivation and drooling from the mouth.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: According to the revised Bio-Medical Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, in which colored container/bag should human anatomical tissue, placenta, and blood-soaked cotton gauze dressings be segregated?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Yellow bags are strictly designated for incinerable organic/pathological wastes: human anatomical tissues, organs, placenta, soiled cotton dressings, and expired cytotoxic drugs.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.optionB: Meticulous hand hygiene (5 moments of hand hygiene)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.optionD: Wearing double gloves for all procedures
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: WHO and CDC establish that proper hand hygiene (alcohol rub for 20–30s or soap & water for 40–60s) is the primary, most cost-effective measure to eliminate pathogen cross-transmission.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the gold standard method to definitively confirm correct placement of a newly inserted nasogastric (NG) tube before initiating enteral feeds or medications?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.optionA: Auscultating air insufflation over the epigastrium with a stethoscope

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: An abdominal/chest X-ray visualizing the tube tip in the stomach below the diaphragm is the absolute gold standard before any feed. Auscultation is unreliable and unsafe.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Left lateral Sims’ position (lying on left side with right knee flexed) aligns with anatomical curvature of sigmoid colon and descending colon, facilitating fluid entry.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A blood pressure cuff with a bladder that is too narrow or applied too loosely on a patient’s arm will result in which measurement error?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: A cuff bladder that is too narrow or wrapped too loosely requires excessive cuff inflation pressure to compress the brachial artery, yielding falsely elevated BP readings.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering an Intramuscular (IM) injection of irritating medications (such as iron dextran) to prevent tracking into subcutaneous tissue, which technique must be employed?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: The Z-track technique displaces skin and subcutaneous tissue laterally before injection, sealing the medication track in the muscle layer upon needle withdrawal and preventing leakage/skin staining.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Beneficence is the ethical duty to do good and promote patient well-being. Non-maleficence is the duty to do no harm; Autonomy is respecting patient decision-making rights.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Ringer Lactate has an electrolyte composition closest to human plasma (Na 130, K 4, Ca 2.7, Cl 109, Lactate 28 mEq/L) and is the frontline crystalloid for shock resuscitation.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Dose = 5 × 70 = 350 mcg/min = 21,000 mcg/hr = 21 mg/hr. Concentration = 400 mg / 250 mL = 1.6 mg/mL. Rate = 21 / 1.6 = 13.125 ≈ 13.1 mL/hr.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Drip rate = (Total Volume in mL × Drop Factor) / Time in Minutes = (1000 × 15) / (8 × 60) = 15,000 / 480 = 31.25 ≈ 31 drops/min.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Protamine sulfate is a strongly basic polycationic peptide that binds ionically to acidic Heparin to form an inactive stable salt complex.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Naloxone is a pure mu-opioid receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression, sedation, and coma.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: N-Acetylcysteine replenishes hepatic glutathione stores, neutralizing the toxic paracetamol metabolite NAPQI (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine).

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Atropine competitively blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors to reverse bronchial secretions and bradycardia, while Pralidoxime reactivates inhibited acetylcholinesterase enzyme.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with Bipolar Disorder is prescribed Lithium Carbonate. What is the narrow therapeutic serum range for maintenance lithium therapy?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with Bipolar Disorder is prescribed Lithium Carbonate. What is the narrow therapeutic serum range for maintenance lithium therapy?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Therapeutic lithium range is 0.6–1.2 mEq/L. Levels > 1.5 mEq/L produce early toxicity (vomiting, coarse tremors, ataxia), and > 2.0 mEq/L can cause seizures, coma, and death.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs is most notorious for causing peripheral neuropathy, which can be prevented by co-prescribing Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs is most notorious for causing peripheral neuropathy, which can be prevented by co-prescribing Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Isoniazid (INH) interferes with vitamin B6 metabolism, leading to dose-dependent peripheral neuropathy. Co-administration of 10–25 mg/day Pyridoxine prevents this adverse effect.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which anti-tubercular medication causes retrobulbar optic neuritis leading to decreased visual acuity and loss of green-red color discrimination?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which anti-tubercular medication causes retrobulbar optic neuritis leading to decreased visual acuity and loss of green-red color discrimination?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Ethambutol (mnemonic: "E" for Eye) is known for ocular toxicity (optic neuritis). Monthly visual acuity and Ishihara color discrimination testing is mandatory.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the primary mechanism of action of Heparin in preventing thrombus formation?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the primary mechanism of action of Heparin in preventing thrombus formation?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.optionA: Accelerating the inhibitory action of Antithrombin III against Thrombin and Factor Xa
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.optionB: Direct inhibition of Vitamin K epoxide reductase
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Heparin binds to antithrombin III, inducing a conformational change that accelerates its inhibition of activated thrombin (Factor IIa) and Factor Xa by over 1000-fold.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the National Immunization Schedule (NIS) of India, what is the exact dose and route for administering BCG vaccine to a neonate at birth?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the National Immunization Schedule (NIS) of India, what is the exact dose and route for administering BCG vaccine to a neonate at birth?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: At birth (up to 4 weeks), BCG vaccine is administered strictly intradermally on left upper arm at a dose of 0.05 mL using a tuberculin syringe (0.1 mL after 1 month).

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At which temperature range must the vaccine cold chain be strictly maintained inside Ice-Lined Refrigerators (ILR) for sensitive vaccines like OPV, Measles, and Pentavalent?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: At which temperature range must the vaccine cold chain be strictly maintained inside Ice-Lined Refrigerators (ILR) for sensitive vaccines like OPV, Measles, and Pentavalent?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: The universal cold chain temperature standard for health facilities and ILRs in India is maintained strictly between +2°C and +8°C at all times.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is epidemiologically expressed as the number of maternal deaths per how many live births in a given year?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is epidemiologically expressed as the number of maternal deaths per how many live births in a given year?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.answerSource: GMCH Chandigarh Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (GMCH CHD Nursing Officer Final Key)
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: MMR is calculated per 100,000 (1 Lakh) live births, whereas Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) and Crude Birth Rate (CBR) are expressed per 1,000 live births.

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which test is utilized in water purification field practice to determine the exact bleaching powder requirement (chlorine demand) to disinfect a water source?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which test is utilized in water purification field practice to determine the exact bleaching powder requirement (chlorine demand) to disinfect a water source?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the population norm for establishing a Primary Health Centre (PHC) in plain areas and hilly/tribal/difficult areas respectively in India?
pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the population norm for establishing a Primary Health Centre (PHC) in plain areas and hilly/tribal/difficult areas respectively in India?

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.explanation: Indian public health norms: Sub-centre = 5,000 (Plain) / 3,000 (Hilly); PHC = 30,000 (Plain) / 20,000 (Hilly); CHC = 120,000 (Plain) / 80,000 (Hilly).

pyq-gmch-chd-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP), what is the overarching target year set by the Government of India to achieve TB elimination in India?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A primigravida at 34 weeks gestation presents with sudden painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. Her vitals are stable and fetal heart rate is 144 bpm. Which nursing action is strictly contraindicated?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.optionB: Establishing wide-bore IV access with Ringer Lactate
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.optionC: Performing a digital vaginal examination (P/V examination)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.optionD: Obtaining an urgent obstetric transabdominal ultrasound
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: In suspected placenta previa (painless bright red bleeding in third trimester), digital vaginal examination is strictly contraindicated as finger insertion can disrupt placental attachments and trigger catastrophic hemorrhage.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: According to Naegele’s rule, what is the expected date of delivery (EDD) for a pregnant woman whose Last Menstrual Period (LMP) was 10 October 2025?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: According to Naegele’s rule, what is the expected date of delivery (EDD) for a pregnant woman whose Last Menstrual Period (LMP) was 10 October 2025?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Naegele’s Rule = LMP + 7 days - 3 months + 1 year. 10 October + 7 days = 17 October; minus 3 months = 17 July 2026.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with severe preeclampsia is receiving an intravenous infusion of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4). Which finding represents early signs of Magnesium toxicity requiring immediate withholding of the infusion?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.optionA: Absence of deep tendon reflexes (Patellar reflex)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Loss of deep tendon reflexes (patellar reflex) is the earliest clinical sign of hypermagnesemia (serum Mg 8–10 mEq/L), preceding respiratory depression (<12/min) and cardiac arrest (>15 mEq/L).

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific, life-saving antidote administered for acute Magnesium Sulfate toxicity in an obstetric patient?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific, life-saving antidote administered for acute Magnesium Sulfate toxicity in an obstetric patient?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.optionA: Calcium Gluconate 10% IV (10 mL slowly over 5–10 minutes)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: 10% Calcium Gluconate (1 g in 10 mL IV push over 3–5 minutes) acts as a direct physiologic antagonist to magnesium at the neuromuscular junction.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the primary frontline drug of choice recommended by WHO guidelines for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) to prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the primary frontline drug of choice recommended by WHO guidelines for active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL) to prevent Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Oxytocin 10 IU IM (or slow IV) immediately after delivery of the baby is the global gold standard uterotonic for AMTSL due to its rapid onset and absence of hypertensive side effects.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A postpartum mother on day 3 post-delivery exhibits normal vaginal discharge that is pinkish-brown in color composed of serous exudate, erythrocytes, and leukocytes. What is this lochia called?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Lochia progression: Lochia Rubra (Days 1–3, red blood); Lochia Serosa (Days 4–10, pink/brownish serous); Lochia Alba (Days 10–21, yellowish-white mucus/leukocytes).

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: During fetal heart rate monitoring, late decelerations are observed following uterine contractions. What is the underlying pathophysiological cause?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: During fetal heart rate monitoring, late decelerations are observed following uterine contractions. What is the underlying pathophysiological cause?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: VEAL CHOP mnemonic: Variable = Cord compression; Early = Head compression; Accelerations = Ok; Late decelerations = Placental insufficiency requiring left lateral positioning, O2, and stopping oxytocin.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A postpartum nurse discovers umbilical cord prolapse protruding through the introitus after membrane rupture. What is the immediate priority nursing action?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Manual upward elevation of the fetal presenting part relieves vascular compression on the prolapsed cord until an emergency cesarean section can be performed.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At which gestational age does the uterine fundus normally reach the level of the maternal umbilicus in a singleton pregnancy?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: At which gestational age does the uterine fundus normally reach the level of the maternal umbilicus in a singleton pregnancy?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Fundal height landmarks: Symphysis pubis = 12 weeks; Midway between pubis & umbilicus = 16 weeks; Umbilicus = 20–22 weeks; Xiphisternum = 36 weeks.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which obstetric sign refers to the bluish or purplish discoloration of the cervix, vagina, and vulva caused by increased venous vascularity during early pregnancy?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Chadwick’s sign is bluish/violet discoloration of vulva/vagina/cervix at ~6–8 weeks. Goodell’s sign is cervical softening; Hegar’s sign is softening of the lower uterine isthmus.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A newborn baby evaluated at 1 minute after birth: Heart rate 110 bpm, slow irregular respirations, active flexed motion, vigorous cry on suctioning, pink body with blue extremities (acrocyanosis). What is the APGAR score?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: The anterior diamond-shaped fontanelle closes between 12 and 18 months of age. The posterior triangular fontanelle (Lambda) closes much earlier, between 6 and 8 weeks (2 months).

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Gross motor milestones: Holds neck steady = 3 months; Sits with support = 5–6 months; Sits without support = 8 months; Stands with support = 9 months; Walks independently = 12–15 months.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.answerSource: IGIMS Patna Nursing Officer Master Answer Key (IGIMS Patna Exam Cell Master Key)
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Phototherapy lights can cause retinal photochemical injury and testicular/gonadal hyperthermic damage, requiring continuous eye shields and diaper coverage.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Hirschsprung disease is congenital aganglionosis of the distal rectum/colon causing functional intestinal obstruction, failure to pass meconium in first 48 hrs, and abdominal distension.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: IMNCI fast breathing thresholds: < 2 months = ≥ 60 breaths/min; 2 to 11 months = ≥ 50 breaths/min; 12 months to 5 years = ≥ 40 breaths/min.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: Viral croup (parainfluenza) causes subglottic tracheal narrowing producing the characteristic "Steeple sign" on frontal neck radiograph, barking cough, and nocturnal stridor.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: The classic "3 Cs" of TEF are Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis during feedings, accompanied by excessive frothy salivation and drooling from the mouth.

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following is the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) including CLABSI and CAUTI?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.optionD: Wearing double gloves for all procedures

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?

pyq-igims-patna-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: By what age does the anterior fontanelle (Bregma) normally close in a healthy developing infant?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: The anterior diamond-shaped fontanelle closes between 12 and 18 months of age. The posterior triangular fontanelle (Lambda) closes much earlier, between 6 and 8 weeks (2 months).

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: At what age does a typically developing infant first achieve the gross motor milestone of sitting steadily without any support?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Gross motor milestones: Holds neck steady = 3 months; Sits with support = 5–6 months; Sits without support = 8 months; Stands with support = 9 months; Walks independently = 12–15 months.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which congenital anomaly is characterized by failure of ganglion cells to migrate to the myenteric plexus of the distal colon, presenting as ribbon-like stools and failure to pass meconium within 48 hours?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Hirschsprung disease is congenital aganglionosis of the distal rectum/colon causing functional intestinal obstruction, failure to pass meconium in first 48 hrs, and abdominal distension.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, what is the fast breathing cut-off defining Pneumonia in an infant aged 2 months to 11 months?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: IMNCI fast breathing thresholds: < 2 months = ≥ 60 breaths/min; 2 to 11 months = ≥ 50 breaths/min; 12 months to 5 years = ≥ 40 breaths/min.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Viral croup (parainfluenza) causes subglottic tracheal narrowing producing the characteristic "Steeple sign" on frontal neck radiograph, barking cough, and nocturnal stridor.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: The classic "3 Cs" of TEF are Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis during feedings, accompanied by excessive frothy salivation and drooling from the mouth.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.optionD: Wearing double gloves for all procedures

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: WHO and CDC establish that proper hand hygiene (alcohol rub for 20–30s or soap & water for 40–60s) is the primary, most cost-effective measure to eliminate pathogen cross-transmission.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: An abdominal/chest X-ray visualizing the tube tip in the stomach below the diaphragm is the absolute gold standard before any feed. Auscultation is unreliable and unsafe.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: When administering a cleansing enema to an adult patient, which position is recommended to facilitate the gravitational flow of the enema solution into the sigmoid colon?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Left lateral Sims’ position (lying on left side with right knee flexed) aligns with anatomical curvature of sigmoid colon and descending colon, facilitating fluid entry.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: The ethical principle that mandates healthcare professionals to act in ways that benefit the patient and promote their physical and emotional well-being is known as:

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Beneficence is the ethical duty to do good and promote patient well-being. Non-maleficence is the duty to do no harm; Autonomy is respecting patient decision-making rights.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which intravenous fluid is isotonic and considered the fluid of resuscitation of choice in acute trauma, hypovolemic shock, and severe dehydration?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Ringer Lactate has an electrolyte composition closest to human plasma (Na 130, K 4, Ca 2.7, Cl 109, Lactate 28 mEq/L) and is the frontline crystalloid for shock resuscitation.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A physician prescribes Dopamine infusion at 5 mcg/kg/min for a patient weighing 70 kg. The IV bag contains 400 mg Dopamine in 250 mL D5W. What should be the infusion pump rate in mL/hr?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Dose = 5 × 70 = 350 mcg/min = 21,000 mcg/hr = 21 mg/hr. Concentration = 400 mg / 250 mL = 1.6 mg/mL. Rate = 21 / 1.6 = 13.125 ≈ 13.1 mL/hr.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: An IV infusion of 1000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a standard macrodrip administration set with a drop factor of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate in drops/minute?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Drip rate = (Total Volume in mL × Drop Factor) / Time in Minutes = (1000 × 15) / (8 × 60) = 15,000 / 480 = 31.25 ≈ 31 drops/min.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific antidote administered to neutralize Heparin-induced severe anticoagulation overdose?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Protamine sulfate is a strongly basic polycationic peptide that binds ionically to acidic Heparin to form an inactive stable salt complex.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the specific competitive receptor antagonist antidote for acute Opioid (Morphine / Fentanyl) overdose presenting with pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Naloxone is a pure mu-opioid receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression, sedation, and coma.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which antidote is administered to prevent acute hepatic necrosis in severe Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: N-Acetylcysteine replenishes hepatic glutathione stores, neutralizing the toxic paracetamol metabolite NAPQI (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine).

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: In Organophosphate / Insecticide poisoning characterized by SLUDGE syndrome (salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis), which drug is the physiological antidote?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A patient with Bipolar Disorder is prescribed Lithium Carbonate. What is the narrow therapeutic serum range for maintenance lithium therapy?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A patient with Bipolar Disorder is prescribed Lithium Carbonate. What is the narrow therapeutic serum range for maintenance lithium therapy?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Therapeutic lithium range is 0.6–1.2 mEq/L. Levels > 1.5 mEq/L produce early toxicity (vomiting, coarse tremors, ataxia), and > 2.0 mEq/L can cause seizures, coma, and death.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs is most notorious for causing peripheral neuropathy, which can be prevented by co-prescribing Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following anti-tubercular drugs is most notorious for causing peripheral neuropathy, which can be prevented by co-prescribing Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Isoniazid (INH) interferes with vitamin B6 metabolism, leading to dose-dependent peripheral neuropathy. Co-administration of 10–25 mg/day Pyridoxine prevents this adverse effect.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which anti-tubercular medication causes retrobulbar optic neuritis leading to decreased visual acuity and loss of green-red color discrimination?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which anti-tubercular medication causes retrobulbar optic neuritis leading to decreased visual acuity and loss of green-red color discrimination?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Ethambutol (mnemonic: "E" for Eye) is known for ocular toxicity (optic neuritis). Monthly visual acuity and Ishihara color discrimination testing is mandatory.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the primary mechanism of action of Heparin in preventing thrombus formation?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the primary mechanism of action of Heparin in preventing thrombus formation?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.optionA: Accelerating the inhibitory action of Antithrombin III against Thrombin and Factor Xa
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.optionB: Direct inhibition of Vitamin K epoxide reductase
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Heparin binds to antithrombin III, inducing a conformational change that accelerates its inhibition of activated thrombin (Factor IIa) and Factor Xa by over 1000-fold.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which of the following defense mechanisms involves redirecting unacceptable impulses, anger, or aggressive feelings toward a less threatening, safer substitute target?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which of the following defense mechanisms involves redirecting unacceptable impulses, anger, or aggressive feelings toward a less threatening, safer substitute target?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Displacement shifts emotional impulses from a threatening source (e.g. boss) to a safer target (e.g. kicking the dog or yelling at family). Sublimation channels impulses into socially constructive activities.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the frontline pharmacological agent prescribed for acute alcohol withdrawal to prevent delirium tremens and withdrawal seizures?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the frontline pharmacological agent prescribed for acute alcohol withdrawal to prevent delirium tremens and withdrawal seizures?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Long-acting benzodiazepines provide cross-tolerance to alcohol at GABA-A receptors, stabilizing autonomic hyperactivity and preventing withdrawal seizures and delirium tremens.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Wernicke-Korsakoff encephalopathy in chronic alcoholism is caused by a severe dietary deficiency of which essential vitamin?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Wernicke-Korsakoff encephalopathy in chronic alcoholism is caused by a severe dietary deficiency of which essential vitamin?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Thiamine (B1) deficiency leads to Wernicke encephalopathy (triad: ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, confusion) and irreversible Korsakoff psychosis (confabulation and amnesia).

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which eating disorder is characterized by recurrent binge eating episodes followed by compensatory purging behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative abuse) with normal or near-normal body weight?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Bulimia nervosa features recurrent binging and inappropriate compensatory purging while maintaining normal weight. Anorexia nervosa is characterized by severe underweight (BMI < 17.5) and body distortion.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Peplau’s interpersonal nursing model outlines four phases: Orientation (problem recognition), Identification, Exploitation/Working (therapeutic interventions), and Resolution/Termination.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: In a clinical research study, the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis when it is actually true (false positive) is known as:

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Type I error (α) occurs when the researcher incorrectly rejects a true null hypothesis. Type II error (β) occurs when a false null hypothesis fails to be rejected (false negative).

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: A train 150 meters long passes a stationary telegraph post in 9 seconds. What is the speed of the train in kilometers per hour (km/h)?
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A train 150 meters long passes a stationary telegraph post in 9 seconds. What is the speed of the train in kilometers per hour (km/h)?

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.answerSource: RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Grade A Master Answer Key (RIMS Ranchi Staff Nurse Screening Key)
pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.explanation: Speed = Distance / Time = 150 m / 9 s = 50/3 m/s. Converting to km/h = (50/3) × (18/5) = 60 km/h.

pyq-rims-ranchi-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: The average age of 24 nursing students in a batch is 21 years. If the age of the nursing tutor is included, the average age increases by 1 year. What is the age of the tutor?

pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.explanation: Naegele’s Rule = LMP + 7 days - 3 months + 1 year. 10 October + 7 days = 17 October; minus 3 months = 17 July 2026.

pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.explanation: IMNCI fast breathing thresholds: < 2 months = ≥ 60 breaths/min; 2 to 11 months = ≥ 50 breaths/min; 12 months to 5 years = ≥ 40 breaths/min.

pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: A 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, and low-grade fever worse at night. The neck X-ray reveals the "Steeple sign". What is the diagnosis?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.answerSource: CNCI Kolkata Staff Nurse (Oncology) Master Answer Key (CNCI Kolkata Official CBT Key)
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.explanation: Viral croup (parainfluenza) causes subglottic tracheal narrowing producing the characteristic "Steeple sign" on frontal neck radiograph, barking cough, and nocturnal stridor.

pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: What is the classic diagnostic triad observed in Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF) with Esophageal Atresia in a newborn at first feed?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.answerSource: CNCI Kolkata Staff Nurse (Oncology) Master Answer Key (CNCI Kolkata Official CBT Key)
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.explanation: The classic "3 Cs" of TEF are Coughing, Choking, and Cyanosis during feedings, accompanied by excessive frothy salivation and drooling from the mouth.

pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Which primitive neonatal reflex is elicited by suddenly lowering the baby’s head or producing a sudden loud sound, resulting in symmetric abduction and extension of arms followed by flexion and cry?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.answerSource: CNCI Kolkata Staff Nurse (Oncology) Master Answer Key (CNCI Kolkata Official CBT Key)
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.explanation: The Moro reflex (startle response) consists of arm abduction/extension followed by adduction/flexion. Asymmetric Moro suggests clavicular fracture or brachial plexus injury (Erb’s palsy).

pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: According to the revised Bio-Medical Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, in which colored container/bag should human anatomical tissue, placenta, and blood-soaked cotton gauze dressings be segregated?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: According to the revised Bio-Medical Waste (Management & Handling) Rules, in which colored container/bag should human anatomical tissue, placenta, and blood-soaked cotton gauze dressings be segregated?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.optionC: Blue cardboard box with blue marking
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.answerSource: CNCI Kolkata Staff Nurse (Oncology) Master Answer Key (CNCI Kolkata Official CBT Key)
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.explanation: Yellow bags are strictly designated for incinerable organic/pathological wastes: human anatomical tissues, organs, placenta, soiled cotton dressings, and expired cytotoxic drugs.

pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextOriginal: Under BMW rules, contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as used IV tubing, Foley catheters, urine bags, and disposable syringes (without needles) must be disposed of in which color bin?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.questionTextDisplay: Under BMW rules, contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as used IV tubing, Foley catheters, urine bags, and disposable syringes (without needles) must be disposed of in which color bin?
pyq-cnci-kolkata-nurse-2026.normalizationNotes: Deterministic OCR text extracted from official source document.
